transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

My head keeps getting stuck on these awful what‑if scenarios about things going wrong with the wiring, and I can’t shut the thoughts off long enough to do my job. It’s incredibly frustrating because I've always been good at my work, but now I just can't seem to clear my mind.
Do you find yourself performing any repetitive behaviors, like checking outlets or appliances over and over, to try to ease the anxiety caused by these thoughts?

Yes, to calm down I'll go back to the same outlet or panel five or ten times—flipping breakers, tugging wires, and re-reading the code book under my breath. I have to do it until I feel this little "click" in my chest that says it's safe. If it doesn't feel just right, I have to start all over again, even if it makes me late or forces me to walk away from the job.
On an average day, about how much time would you say you spend dealing with these thoughts and performing these checking routines?

I'm not really sure of the exact amount of time because I've never actually timed it. It feels like it consumes a huge portion of my day, though, and it keeps me up late into the night. It just feels like it's taking over most of my waking hours.
Would you say that the repetitive thoughts themselves and the physical checking behaviors are equally troublesome for you, or does one of them cause you much more distress than the other?

They are chained together, so they torture me in different ways. The terrifying thoughts of a house burning down are mentally agonizing and drive me to check, but the physical checking is what actually ruins my life. That constant re-checking is what makes me late, stops me from finishing my work, and causes me to lose jobs.
How long have you been experiencing these distressing thoughts and the need to repeatedly check things—has it been going on for at least a few weeks or months?

It's been going on for much longer than just a few weeks. I've always been meticulous, but these severe thoughts and the constant re-checking really escalated and took over after my marital separation and move to my apartment, which was several months ago.
Do you recognize these thoughts as coming from your own mind, and do you ever try to resist the urge to do the checking, even if it's difficult to stop?

I'm not really sure how to describe where the thoughts come from, they just feel like they completely take over my brain. As for resisting, the anxiety gets so overwhelming that I feel like I have absolutely no choice but to check just to make it go away.

These symptoms have been present for several months and cause significant distress and functional impairment. This presentation aligns perfectly with F42.2 (Mixed obsessive-compulsive acts and thoughts). Sufficient evidence has been gathered to make a confident diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with both prominent obsessional thoughts (intrusive fears of electrical failure and house fires) and compulsive behaviors (repetitive checking of outlets, breakers, and code books). These symptoms are closely linked, highly time-consuming, and cause significant functional impairment, leading to difficulties at work. Because both obsessions and compulsions are present and clinically significant, F42.2 (Mixed obsessional thoughts and acts) is the most accurate diagnosis.
